chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a newborn who has neither what belongs to men nor what belongs to women. He said: The Imam or the one casting lots writes 'Abdullah' on one lot and 'Ummullah' on another lot. Then the Imam or the caster says: 'O God, You are the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You judge between Your servants regarding that in which they differ. Make clear to us the matter of this newborn, how he is to be inherited with what You have prescribed for him in the Book.' Then the two lots are thrown among ambiguous lots, and the lot is cast upon what comes out, and he is inherited according to it. And we have narrated other similar narrations in our Great Book, so this does not contradict them.
What Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Muhammad and Ahmad, sons of al-Hasan, from their father from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from some of our companions from them (peace be upon him):

About a newborn who has neither what belongs to men nor what belongs to women, except a hole from which urine comes out. Regarding which inheritance he is to be inherited: He said: If when he urinates his urine moves aside (is distinct), he is inherited as one of the males; and if his urine does not move aside, he is inherited as a female. This does not contradict the first narrations because they are understood to apply when there is no way to know whether he is male or female, so casting lots is used. But if it is possible [to know], then acting upon the last narration is not prohibited, even if taking the first narrations is more cautious and preferable.
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yusuf ibn Aqil from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him):

He said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a slave girl whom her master had intercourse with during the period of her purity, then he sold her to another before she menstruated. The second man had intercourse with her, and she had not yet menstruated. Both men had intercourse with her in one period of purity, and she gave birth to a boy. They disputed over him, and the mother of the boy was asked. She said: Both of them came to me in one period of purity, and I do not know which one is his father. He ruled regarding the boy that he inherits both of them that the boy inherits from both of them, and they both inherit from him equally.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: We have clarified in what preceded from the Book that if a girl is penetrated by a group in one period of purity after she has passed from the first to the second through sale, the child is attached to the one who possesses the girl. And if they are partners and penetrate her in one period of purity, the child is determined by casting lots; whoever the lot falls upon, the child is attached to him, and he guarantees the value of the share of the others. The reason for this report is that we carry it upon a type of precautionary dissimulation (taqiyyah) because it agrees with some of the schools of the Sunnis.
ai.seo_question: How is the gender and inheritance of a hermaphrodite determined in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar elucidates the Shia jurisprudence of *mawlud* (hermaphrodite), distinguishing between cases where gender is determined by physical signs (urine flow) versus those requiring *qur'a* (casting lots) by the Imam. It further addresses paternity disputes in slave women, citing Imam al-Baqir's ruling on equal inheritance from two men who had intercourse in the same purity period, while noting the scholarly view that this may reflect *taqiyya* to align with Sunni methodologies.
